title: A Language-Guided Multimodal Foundation Model for Zero-Shot and Multi-Task Brain Signal Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2609.15740v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Brain signal analysis is essential for both neuroscience research and clinical diagnostics, yet current approaches face critical limitations. End-to-end models require task-specific retraining and exhibit limited generalization, while pre-trained models lack semantic depth and still depend on extensive fine-tuning. Meanwhile, general-purpose multimodal foundation models, though powerful in other domains, struggle to interpret brain signals due to representational misalignment and lack of domain knowledge. This study introduces a multimodal foundation model for zero-shot and multi-task brain signal analysis (METIS) through a unified language-signal alignment framework. METIS is pretrained on the largest and most diverse brain-signal corpus to date, comprising over 70,000 h of recordings from more than 11,000 subjects across 20 datasets. In a comprehensive zero-shot evaluation across 12 datasets, METIS outperformed the leading generalist

translated_title: 一种用于零样本和多任务脑信号分析的语言引导多模态基础模型
translated_abstract: 脑信号分析对神经科学研究和临床诊断都至关重要，然而当前方法面临关键局限。端到端模型需要针对特定任务重新训练且泛化能力有限，而预训练模型缺乏语义深度且仍依赖大量微调。与此同时，通用多模态基础模型虽然在其他领域表现强大，但由于表征不对齐和缺乏领域知识，难以解读脑信号。本研究通过统一的语言-信号对齐框架，提出了一个面向零样本和多任务脑信号分析的多模态基础模型（METIS）。METIS在迄今为止规模最大、最多样化的脑信号语料库上进行预训练，该语料库包含来自20个数据集、超过11,000名受试者的超过70,000小时的记录。在涵盖12个数据集的全面零样本评估中，METIS的表现超越了领先的通用基础模型。
tldr: 本研究提出METIS，一个基于语言-信号对齐框架的多模态基础模型，在超过70,000小时的脑信号数据上预训练，首次实现了零样本和多任务脑信号分析，并超越了领先的通用模型。
